```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The maternal mortality file used in Week 3 has one row per country and one
column per year. `prepare_mortality()` turns those year columns into rows for
joining to other country-year data.

```{r}
library(pivotwbmilly)
dim(maternal_mortality)
maternal_mortality[maternal_mortality$iso == "CAN",
                   c("iso", "X2000", "X2017", "X2018", "X2019")]
```

The example has 186 countries and 22 columns: a country code, an indicator
description, and 20 year columns. Values are maternal deaths per 100,000 live
births. All 2018 and 2019 values are missing in the supplied extract.

```{r}
maternal_long <- prepare_mortality(maternal_mortality, "maternal_mortality")
dim(maternal_long)
head(maternal_long)
sum(is.na(maternal_long$maternal_mortality))
```

The output has 3,720 rows and three columns. It keeps all 426 missing values.
Each country still has 20 rows, even if some years have no reported value.

For an analysis restricted to a few years, pass them in `years` and choose a
shorter measure name if needed:

```{r}
recent <- prepare_mortality(maternal_mortality, "mmr", years = 2015:2017)
recent[recent$iso == "CAN", ]
```

The same function accepts the infant, neonatal, and under-five mortality tables
from Week 3 because they use the same `iso` and `XYYYY` columns. It returns the
measure column under the name passed in `outcome_name`.

Missing year columns and repeated country codes cause an error. For example,
requesting 2020 fails because that column is absent:

```{r}
tryCatch(
  prepare_mortality(maternal_mortality, "mmr", years = 2020),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
```

This package performs the reshape only. Country exclusions, imputations, and
the conflict and covariate joins remain separate analytical decisions.
